strengths_note: Per-regiment present-for-duty strengths and Confederate regimental strengths were not found. Mounted strength was well below paper strength on both sides (inferred). Not found: Confederate regimental strengths, horse artillery gun counts for most batteries, Jenkins' movements June 26-July 2.

carbines.printed: Buford's July 1 screen carried a mix: Sharps (most common; .52 or .54 linen cartridge), Burnside (.54 tapered brass), Gallager (.52 brass, hard to extract), Smith (.50 rubber cartridge, well regarded), Merrill (.54 paper, fragile and unpopular) and Sharps & Hankins (.52 rimfire; three companies of the 9th NY). The cartridges were not interchangeable. The belief that Buford's troopers had Spencers on July 1 is folklore (Civil War News, Bilby, "Carbine Folklore").
carbines.other: Other carbine facts: Sharps was the most common Union cavalry arm by 1863 (about 90,000 carbines; .52, 475 gr, 50 gr powder; 8-10 rounds/min); Burnside .54 with a 21 in barrel, 7 lb, 43 Union cavalry regiments in 1863-64; Spencer rifle 47 in overall (30 in barrel) with 7-round tube, .56-56. The Spencer carbine was not produced until October 1863 (AR, Civil War News), which seems to conflict with Spencer use on July 3: inferred explanation is rifle versus carbine models, to be verified. Henry rifles are not documented at Gettysburg. Shortages of Sharps carbines were noted (Ripley letter of June 2). Specifications for Gallager, Smith, Merrill, Starr, Joslyn, Maynard and Sharps & Hankins were not retrieved.
carbines.folklore: Spencers on Buford's line July 1 = folklore

horses.detail: About 17,000 remounts to the Union Cavalry Corps May-July 1863; horses under 6 years accepted from June 1 and many broke down; hard pikes wore out shoes quickly; bad contractor saddles ruined backs
Pleasonton lost about 1,000 horses at Brandy Station (estimate)
10th NY 303 serviceable and 191 unserviceable for 460 men; 6th US about 500 serviceable of about 1,072 assigned; an 8th NY company 56 men with 43 horses

Buford "Grey Eagle" (old, white); Custer lost two horses on July 3 (second in the 1st Michigan melee; the first at the Rummel fence, replaced by a bugler's horse) and had another shot at Hunterstown; Stuart's horses exhausted
Exhausted horses; Dover capture of more than 1,000 horses

arrival_rule_facts: Fixed facts for the arrival rule: the Michigan Brigade and Farnsworth's brigade fought at Hanover June 30 and Hunterstown July 2, then moved to East Cavalry Field and South Cavalry Field on July 3; the 2nd Brigade of Gregg's division (Huey) was at Westminster and never at Gettysburg; the 35th Va Bn was with Early's infantry, not with the main cavalry; Stuart's three brigades reached the field after the first day.
